root_cause.text: The mt7925 remain-on-channel abort path incorrectly called cancel_work_sync() on roc_work while the caller could already hold dev->mt76.mutex, causing a self-deadlock because roc_work also runs under that same mutex in the mt76/mt7925 ROC state handling.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE and commit message explicitly state that “roc_work() holds dev->mt76.mutex, while cancel_work_sync() waits for roc_work() to finish” and that this happens in the station-removal path leading to mt7925_roc_abort_sync(); the patch removes cancel_work_sync(), first atomically clears MT76_STATE_ROC with test_and_clear_bit(), and replaces it with cancel_work() to avoid waiting while preserving single ownership.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix ROC abort handling by clearing the ROC state before teardown, skipping inactive aborts, and resuming interfaces after non-blocking work cancellation.
intent_record.what: The function now checks `test_and_clear_bit(MT76_STATE_ROC, &phy->mt76->state)` at the start and returns immediately if the ROC state bit was not set. It removes the later conditional `if (test_and_clear_bit(...))` block, changes `cancel_work_sync(&phy->roc_work)` to `cancel_work(&phy->roc_work)`, and makes `ieee80211_iterate_interfaces(..., mt7925_roc_iter, (void *)phy)` run unconditionally after the timer deletion and work cancellation.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now aborts only once per active ROC session by atomically clearing the ROC state up front and exiting early if no ROC is active. When ROC is active, it always deletes the timer, schedules cancellation of the ROC work without waiting synchronously for completion, and always resumes interfaces afterward. This avoids repeated abort handling and changes the synchronization behavior by no longer blocking on pending ROC work completion.

grouping_result.intent: Fix ROC abort handling by clearing the ROC state before teardown, skipping inactive aborts, and resuming interfaces after non-blocking work cancellation.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly targets the ROC abort path and avoids the problematic synchronous cancellation pattern by clearing ROC state, skipping inactive aborts, and using non-blocking cancellation/resume handling, which addresses the deadlock root cause in ROC teardown under the shared mutex.

candidates.rationale: This synchronous work cancellation is the direct cause of the self-deadlock: the abort path may be invoked while dev->mt76.mutex is already held, and roc_work itself runs under that same mutex, so waiting synchronously for roc_work can deadlock.

vuln_statements.explanation: This synchronous cancellation waits for roc_work to finish. In the remain-on-channel abort path, the caller may already hold dev->mt76.mutex, while roc_work also executes under that same mutex, creating a self-deadlock when cancel_work_sync() waits on work that cannot complete.

bic_trace_step.reason:
The snippet is sufficient because it shows the exact remain-on-channel abort helper added in this commit and its call site. The vulnerable construct is present in `mt7925_roc_abort_sync()`:

- `cancel_work_sync(&phy->roc_work);`

The stated root cause is calling `cancel_work_sync()` on `roc_work` while the caller may already hold `dev->mt76.mutex`, which can self-deadlock because `roc_work` runs under that same mutex. This helper is then invoked from `mt7925_mac_link_sta_remove()` via:

- `mt7925_roc_abort_sync(dev);`

There is no visible protection or alternative handling here to avoid the deadlock condition—no check that the mutex is not held, no deferred/asynchronous cancellation, and no special unlock/relock pattern. Therefore the vulnerable logic is present.

The fix is not present in this snippet because the code still directly uses `cancel_work_sync(&phy->roc_work)` in the ROC abort path. So this commit version contains the bug and does not yet contain the deadlock-preventing fix.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant ROC abort and ROC work logic is fully visible in this snippet. The vulnerable construct is present in `mt7925_abort_roc()`, which does `del_timer_sync(&phy->roc_timer);` followed by `cancel_work_sync(&phy->roc_work);` before taking the mutex. The root cause says the abort path must not call `cancel_work_sync()` on `roc_work` when the caller may already hold `dev->mt76.mutex`, because `roc_work` itself runs under that same mutex. The work function shown here, `mt7925_roc_work()`, explicitly acquires that mutex: `mt792x_mutex_acquire(phy->dev); ... mt792x_mutex_release(phy->dev);`. Also, callers can invoke the abort path while holding the mutex: `mt7925_mgd_complete_tx()` calls `mt7925_abort_roc()` directly, and `mt7925_mgd_prepare_tx()` / other ROC paths show this logic is tied to the same state machinery; moreover `mt7925_remain_on_channel()` and `mt7925_set_roc()` operate under `mt792x_mutex_acquire(phy->dev)`, demonstrating ROC handling is mutex-based. There is no protective logic in `mt7925_abort_roc()` to avoid `cancel_work_sync()` when the mutex is already held, nor any alternative non-blocking cancellation. Therefore the bug is present and the fix is not yet included.
